parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State how, in a modern X-ray tube, the intensity of the X-ray beam and its hardness are controlled.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
A model of a limb consists of soft tissue and bone, as illustrated in Fig. 11.1.

[[fig:f1]]

The soft tissue has a thickness of 9.0 cm. The bone within the soft tissue has a thickness of 3.0 cm.

Data for the linear attenuation (absorption) coefficient μ of X-rays in soft tissue and in bone are shown in Table 11.1.

[[fig:f2]]

A parallel beam of X-rays of intensity *I*₀ is incident normally on the model.

Calculate, in terms of *I*₀:
parts.text: the transmitted intensity *I*ₛ through soft tissue alone

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the transmitted intensity *I*꜀ through soft tissue and bone.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: By reference to your answers in (b), suggest, with a reason, whether good contrast on an X-ray image would be obtained.

figures.caption: Fig. 11.1
figures.alt: A limb model with a central bone surrounded by soft tissue, with incident and transmitted X-ray beams and thickness dimensions marked.

figures.caption: Table 11.1
figures.alt: A table giving the linear attenuation coefficient in cm⁻¹ as 0.92 for soft tissue and 2.9 for bone.
